payload.question_text: Which statements describe AzureKeyCredential and TextAnalyticsClient? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: AzureKeyCredential provides API-key credentials for authenticated Azure SDK access. It supplies the key when creating the client.

options.text: TextAnalyticsClient is a deployed model name
options.error_type: Confuses client object with model deployment
options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is a client class used for Azure Language analysis. A deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the name assigned to a deployed general-purpose model.

feedback.intrinsic: A developer would look for a model deployment instead of creating the Azure Language client needed to make requests.
feedback.instructional: TextAnalyticsClient is the client; a deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model.

options.text: TextAnalyticsClient is an Azure Language client
options.rationale: TextAnalyticsClient is the Python client for Azure Language text analysis. Its methods call Azure Language capabilities.
AzureKeyCredential supplies an API key for authenticated access. It does not perform any text analysis.
options.better_fit: Choose this for detect_language(), which detects language details.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would have credentials but would not make a language-detection request.
feedback.instructional: Use AzureKeyCredential for access and detect_language() for language analysis.

payload.explanation: Correct. AzureKeyCredential provides access credentials, and TextAnalyticsClient calls Azure Language capabilities.

payload.question_text: What is the Azure Language SDK?

options.text: A library for deployed OpenAI models
options.error_type: Confuses Azure Language SDK with OpenAI Python library
options.rationale: This describes the OpenAI Python library, which interacts with OpenAI models and services. It is not the Azure Language client library.
options.better_fit: Choose this when Python code must interact with OpenAI models and services.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing this would focus the developer on model access instead of the purpose-built language features needed.
feedback.instructional: Keep the libraries separate: Azure Language SDK is for Azure Language capabilities, while the OpenAI Python library connects to OpenAI models.

options.rationale: A general-purpose model follows prompts and can handle many language tasks. An SDK is ready-made code used to call capabilities from an application.
options.better_fit: Choose this for flexible, prompt-based analysis such as summarizing or answering questions.

feedback.intrinsic: This choice would not identify the code library needed to add language detection or PII redaction.
feedback.instructional: A model analyzes language; the Azure Language SDK is the client library that lets an application use Azure Language features.

options.rationale: The portal is a web interface for building, testing, and deploying applications. The SDK is used in application code.
options.better_fit: Choose this when referring to the web interface used to build, test, and deploy applications.

feedback.intrinsic: This would send someone to a browser interface when the task calls for code integration.
feedback.instructional: Use the portal to explore and manage work; use the Azure Language SDK inside an application.

options.text: A client library for Azure Language features
options.rationale: This is ready-made developer code for adding Azure Language capabilities to an application. It supports features such as language detection and PII redaction.

payload.explanation: Correct. The Azure Language SDK is a client library that adds Azure Language capabilities to applications.

payload.question_text: TextAnalyticsClient can be created with an endpoint and AzureKeyCredential(key).

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Without both parts, the client configuration described here is incomplete.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Create TextAnalyticsClient with the endpoint and AzureKeyCredential(key).

payload.explanation: Correct. The client is configured with the Azure Language endpoint and an API-key credential.

payload.question_text: The Azure Language SDK can add language detection and PII redaction to an application.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That choice would overlook two key capabilities available through the library.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The Azure Language SDK supports language detection and PII detection with redaction.

payload.explanation: Correct. These are Azure Language capabilities that the SDK can add to an application.

payload.question_text: An AI agent is connected to an Azure Language MCP server to analyze customer feedback. Which statements correctly describe this connection? Select all that apply.

options.text: The agent can be the MCP client
options.rationale: An AI agent, or the host application running it, can be the MCP client. The client sends requests and receives responses.

options.text: The client must expose server tools
options.error_type: Reverses MCP client and server roles
options.rationale: The server exposes capabilities for the client to discover and invoke. The client sends requests rather than exposing the server's capabilities.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the MCP server, which exposes tools, data, or actions.

feedback.intrinsic: Reversing the roles would make it unclear where the agent should send its request.
feedback.instructional: Remember the direction: client requests; server exposes capabilities and returns structured results.

options.text: The client sends requests and receives responses
options.rationale: Sending requests and receiving responses is the client's role. This can be the agent or host application.

options.text: The server exposes tools or data
options.rationale: The MCP server exposes capabilities, data, or actions. It runs the requested capability and returns a structured result.

payload.explanation: Correct. In MCP, the client requests capabilities and the server exposes them and returns structured results.

payload.question_text: What can recognize_pii_entities() return? Select all that apply.

options.error_type: Confuses PII detection with language detection
options.rationale: A primary language ISO code comes from language detection. PII detection instead returns redacted text and entity details.
options.better_fit: Choose this for detect_language(), which returns the ISO 639-1 code.

feedback.intrinsic: This would confuse a privacy result with a value used to identify and route languages.
feedback.instructional: Use recognize_pii_entities() for redaction and entity details; use detect_language() for the primary-language ISO code.

options.rationale: The result contains a redacted version of the input. This supports sharing content after personal details are hidden.
Each detected entity includes its text. This lets code report what was found.
Each entity includes a category and confidence score. These details describe the detected personal information.

payload.explanation: Correct. PII detection returns redacted content and details about the personal entities it finds.

payload.question_text: The managed Azure Language MCP server exposes Azure Language features through MCP.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would miss how an agent reaches managed Azure Language capabilities through MCP.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The managed Azure Language MCP server exposes Azure Language features, including named entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and language detection.

payload.explanation: Correct. It bridges an agent to Azure Language capabilities through the MCP standard.

payload.question_text: What is MCP?

options.text: A Python library for Azure Language
options.rationale: The Azure Language SDK is a Python client library. MCP is an open connection standard for agents and external capabilities.
options.better_fit: Choose this description for the Azure Language SDK.

feedback.intrinsic: This would lead someone to look for application code instead of a standard connection approach for agents.
feedback.instructional: MCP is a protocol, while the Azure Language SDK is a client library.

options.text: An open standard for agent tool connections
options.rationale: MCP defines a standard way for agents to connect to external capabilities and data sources. It avoids custom integration code for every service.

options.text: A client object for text analysis
options.rationale: A client object is a specific object created to call a service. MCP defines how clients and servers communicate.
options.better_fit: Choose this for TextAnalyticsClient, the Azure Language Python client.

feedback.intrinsic: The roles in a client-server connection would remain unclear.
feedback.instructional: MCP is the shared protocol; TextAnalyticsClient is a client used for Azure Language analysis.

options.rationale: A deployment name identifies a deployed general-purpose model. MCP is unrelated to naming a model deployment.
options.better_fit: Choose this when referring to the name assigned during deployment of a general-purpose model.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would name a model rather than establish the shared connection approach it needs.
feedback.instructional: MCP connects agents with external capabilities; a deployment name identifies a deployed model.

payload.explanation: Correct. MCP is an open standard that lets agents connect to external capabilities and data sources.

payload.question_text: recognize_pii_entities() identifies personal details and can return redacted text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would leave out the method's key privacy purpose.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: recognize_pii_entities() identifies personal details and returns redacted text plus information about detected entities.

payload.explanation: Correct. The method identifies PII and provides a redacted result along with entity details.

payload.question_text: What does detect_language() return for a text string? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The result includes the primary language name. Code can read it from primary_language.name.
The result includes the language's ISO 639-1 code. Code can read it from primary_language.iso6391_name.
The result includes a confidence score between 0 and 1. This shows confidence in the detected language.

options.error_type: Confuses language detection with PII detection
options.rationale: Redacted text is returned by PII detection. Language detection returns language details and confidence instead.
options.better_fit: Choose this for recognize_pii_entities(), which returns a redacted version of the input.

feedback.intrinsic: Selecting this would mix privacy output with language-routing output.
feedback.instructional: Keep the methods distinct: detect_language() returns language details; recognize_pii_entities() returns redacted text.

payload.explanation: Correct. The method returns a language name, ISO 639-1 code, and confidence score.

payload.question_text: MCP requires custom integration code for every external service an agent uses.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: That approach would recreate the per-service work MCP is intended to avoid.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: MCP acts like a universal adapter: an agent can connect to an MCP server that exposes capabilities in a standard way.

payload.explanation: Correct. MCP provides a standard connection approach instead of custom integration for every service.

payload.question_text: detect_language() returns redacted text and PII entity categories.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would mix the results used for privacy handling with the results used for language routing.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: detect_language() returns language name, ISO 639-1 code, and confidence score. recognize_pii_entities() returns redacted text and PII details.

payload.explanation: Correct. Those results belong to PII detection, not language detection.

evidence.statement: The selected answers and explanations align with the source: AzureKeyCredential supplies the API key, TextAnalyticsClient is the Azure Language client, and the SDK supports Azure Language capabilities.
The MCP, language-detection, and PII-detection claims match the authoritative source material.
Each item has a clearly keyed answer; multi-select items identify all and only the source-supported statements, while true/false items make a single claim with an explicit answer.
Distractors are credible role or capability confusions, such as confusing TextAnalyticsClient with a deployment name, MCP with an SDK, or language detection with PII redaction.
Wrong options diagnose realistic misconceptions: reversing MCP client/server roles, treating an SDK as a model or portal, and assigning redaction output to detect_language().
The ordered session moves from foundational SDK and credential identification into client construction, MCP roles, method outputs, and agent integration concepts.
The sequence includes some topic interleaving and returns to related methods, so progression is coherent but not strongly cumulative toward an end-to-end agent task.

The 12-item sequence alternates multiple choice, multi-select, and true/false mechanics with no long uninterrupted run of one mechanic; the main repetition is the opening pair of multiple-choice items and adjacent true/false pairs.
Stems vary across identification, capability, construction, role, return-value, and requirement forms, although several begin with recurring patterns such as “What” or a method name.
Most items are decontextualized definitions or API-output checks rather than credible developer decisions; the MCP item tests roles directly without placing the learner in an agent integration task.
Incorrect-option feedback identifies the misconception and gives a corrective distinction or next step, such as using AzureKeyCredential for access and detect_language() for analysis.
True/false items provide concise corrective instruction distinguishing the relevant method, capability, or client/server role.
The session is labeled Level 1 and appropriately emphasizes remembering and understanding foundational SDK, MCP, language-detection, and PII concepts rather than advanced implementation.

The artifact consistently distinguishes Azure Language SDK, TextAnalyticsClient, AzureKeyCredential, MCP client/server, detect_language(), and recognize_pii_entities() in the same roles used by the source.

The exact sequence is deterministic, source-faithful, varied in mechanics, and supported by targeted corrective feedback; its main experiential weakness is that it rarely asks learners to apply the concepts in a realistic agent or application task.
